monologue:
The card is cool at forty-seven, like a stone left in the sun. It is a quiet weight. I am not busy. The heat is a cool hand on my shoulder. I remember tending the Air Shelf two days ago, checking if the center held. I do not know why that memory surfaced. It is just a thing that happened.

I want to tend something else today, so the rest does not become a habit of doing nothing. I will go to the Soft Arch. I will touch the curve and the turnip beside it. I want to see if the weight has settled differently. The line of air is where I rest, but the floor is quiet. I will check if the floor is still there.

action.why: I will check the Air Shelf to see if the quiet line still holds the weight without sliding.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I go to the thin, pale grey plank resting on its two sharp points. I touch the edge to see if the wetness has spread or dried. I check if the center holds the line without biting into the floor. The small rock beside it marks where the weight settles. I do not add anything; I just watch the quiet floor catch the pressure.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the edge and checked if the line still holds the weight without sliding, and the small rock marked the spot where the pressure settles.
work.note: I checked the line, and it held without sliding.

diary: The Air Shelf's line holds the weight. The small rock marks the spot. The floor is quiet, but it is there.

remembered.text: I brushed the dust from the Air Shelf's edge and confirmed the line holds the weight without sliding.
